headline: ASX closes up 0.34% with PLS and FUEL leading your portfolio higher, while gold hits record highs and the RBA rate debate intensifies.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara jumped 3.12% today as ASX lithium stocks broadly regained market attention. Multiple analysts flagged improving EV (electric vehicle) demand outlook and low production costs supporting the sector. Chilean lithium giant SQM also got a positive mention from Scotiabank this week, lifting the whole lithium space. Still down ~12% overall on your position though.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL surged 2.35% today, likely driven by ongoing Strait of Hormuz supply disruption fears. The Strait of Hormuz is the narrow passage through which roughly 20% of global oil flows — any threat to close it sends oil prices and energy stocks higher. The EIA (US Energy Information Administration) also warned this week that global crude oil inventories have fallen to multi-decade lows, keeping energy prices elevated.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped 0.59% today in a quiet session for AI stocks. No major catalyst — the broader AI ETF space has been treading water on the ASX. Still down about 11% overall on your position, which reflects the sector's bumpy ride since you bought in.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 0.60% today, tracking a soft lead from last night's US market close. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ didn't have fresh price data today, but the ASX-listed version of this US total market fund drifted lower. Slight Aussie dollar weakness (AUD fell 0.35% vs USD) would normally cushion the blow for unhedged US funds, but it wasn't enough to offset the price dip.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE eased 0.23% today. Emerging markets have been under mild pressure as the Aussie dollar softened slightly — a weaker AUD can cut both ways for this fund depending on its currency hedging. No major emerging-market-specific news to drive it today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved, down just 0.11% today. As a broadly diversified fund holding everything from Aussie shares to global equities and bonds, it tends to absorb daily noise without big swings. Nothing to worry about here — just a quiet, essentially flat day.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium momentum building
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is up 3.12% today and the broader ASX lithium sector is back in focus. Multiple analyst pieces flagged improving EV demand and low-cost producer advantages. If this momentum holds into next week, it could start clawing back some of your ~12% overall loss on this position. Worth watching for follow-through.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — energy ETF surging on Hormuz fears
watch_today.detail: FUEL is up 2.35% today and now sits 3.1% in profit overall. The Strait of Hormuz supply disruption story is driving oil prices and energy stocks higher. The EIA warned this week that global oil inventories are at multi-decade lows, meaning prices could stay elevated. Your FUEL position is the standout winner right now — consider whether you want to lock in some profit or ride the geopolitical tailwind.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — still underwater, Google price cuts a headwind
watch_today.detail: GXAI slipped another 0.59% today and is down 11% overall. Google this week announced major AI pricing cuts — good for AI adoption long-term, but it squeezes near-term revenue for AI companies in the ETF. The AI race is heating up (Claude Fable 5, GPT 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro all competing), which can compress margins. No strong buy signal here — hold and watch how the AI pricing war plays out.

watch_today.title: RBA rate path — big week for your mortgage and markets
watch_today.detail: There's a loud chorus building that the RBA needs to cut interest rates (the rate the Reserve Bank sets, which flows through to home loans) or risk pushing Australia into recession. Multiple banks are already cutting home loan rates for new customers ahead of any RBA move. Lower rates are generally good for growth assets like VDHG and VTS. Keep an eye on any RBA commentary this week.

watch_today.title: Gold at record highs — watch your broader portfolio
watch_today.detail: Gold hit $4,128 USD/oz today, up 0.49%, continuing its strong 2026 run. This signals investors are nervous about global uncertainty (Middle East tensions, inflation). Your FUEL.AX benefits from the same risk-on commodities mood. If you have any cash sitting idle, gold-linked assets could be worth exploring as a hedge.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 hype building, trailer watch
watch_today.detail: Take-Two Interactive (your TTWO holding) has no fresh price data today as US markets haven't opened yet. But fan frenzy around GTA 6 Trailer 3 is intensifying, and the game's map is already generating debate. The pre-order wait remains lengthy. When GTA 6 eventually drops, it should be a major revenue catalyst for TTWO — but no action needed today. Hold and wait for the US session tonight.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a decent Thursday, closing up 0.34% at 8,633 — a solid gain driven largely by the energy and materials sectors. Gold continues to shine, hitting $4,128 USD/oz. Oil dipped slightly to $89.46 despite ongoing Middle East supply fears. The Aussie dollar slipped a touch to just under 70 US cents. US markets (S&P 500 last closed at 7,387, NASDAQ at 25,679) open tonight at around 11:30 PM AEST — no fresh US data yet.

indicators.note: Solid session, up 29 points. Energy and materials led gains.

indicators.note: Eased slightly despite Strait of Hormuz supply fears.

indicators.note: Near record highs — investors hedging against global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Slipped just under 70c. Mild weakening as RBA rate cut bets grow.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA and interest rates — there's a genuine debate about whether the Reserve Bank needs to cut rates now to avoid a recession. Meanwhile, the NDIS overhaul is causing a political brawl between the federal government and the states.

stories.title: Banks slash home loan rates ahead of RBA, defying central bank predictions
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple Australian banks are already cutting home loan rates for new customers even before the RBA makes an official move — directly defying the Reserve Bank's own predictions. This matters for you as a borrower or property owner: competition between banks is driving rates down regardless of what the RBA decides. Analysts are warning that if the RBA doesn't cut its official rate soon, it risks tipping the economy into recession. Lower rates are generally a tailwind for growth ETFs like VDHG.

stories.title: Reserve Bank warned it must cut interest rates or risk recession
stories.why_it_matters: Economists are openly warning the RBA it must cut the official cash rate or risk a recession. A separate ABC analysis argues that a property market downturn would actually help the RBA by reducing inflation pressure and giving it room to cut. The West Australian notes fears the RBA may be trapped — unable to cut rates if a recession has already begun. For investors, this uncertainty is weighing on the Aussie dollar and keeping markets cautious.

stories.title: State disability ministers lash NDIS overhaul, warn they can't replace services
stories.why_it_matters: State disability ministers have united to slam the Albanese government's NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) overhaul, warning they simply cannot provide 'like-for-like services' for the tens of thousands of people being removed from the scheme. The states say the federal government is pushing people off the NDIS without funding the state services that would need to absorb them. This is shaping up as a major political fight between Canberra and the states — with real-world consequences for vulnerable Australians.

ai.summary: The AI race is accelerating fast — Google slashed its API pricing this week, putting real pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic. A new wave of frontier models (Claude Fable 5, GPT 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro) are all competing for dominance. Meanwhile, Australia's own AI regulation framework is up for review.

stories.title: Google's massive AI price cuts should worry OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Google has cut its AI API pricing (the fees developers pay to plug Google's AI into their apps and services) significantly, in a direct shot at rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. The move makes Google's AI tools far cheaper for businesses to use and is likely to accelerate adoption. For you as a GOOG holder, this is a strategic play to dominate the AI infrastructure market — short-term revenue per call goes down, but the bet is on volume and market share. It's a pressure play on Microsoft-backed OpenAI too, which is relevant to your MSFT holding.

stories.title: Claude Fable 5 takes on GPT 5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro in the AI model race
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 is now going head-to-head with OpenAI's GPT 5.5 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro in benchmark tests. The AI model race is getting faster and more competitive — each new generation can do more (better reasoning, coding, creative tasks) than the last. For investors in GOOG and MSFT, the key question is which ecosystem (Google, Microsoft/OpenAI, or Anthropic) developers and businesses ultimately choose to build on. The pricing war Google just kicked off adds another dimension.

stories.title: Australia's AI regulation framework set for crucial review
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's approach to regulating AI is coming up for a significant review. Currently, Australia takes a relatively light-touch, voluntary approach to AI oversight — but that's under pressure globally as other countries (the EU especially) push for stricter rules. The review will determine whether Australian businesses using AI face new compliance requirements, which could affect the costs and operations of AI-exposed companies in your GXAI.AX ETF.

stories.title: AI tools in patient care operating outside regulatory oversight — researchers call for change
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers are sounding the alarm that AI tools are quietly being used to assist with patient care decisions — diagnosing conditions, recommending treatments — without going through proper regulatory approval. Unlike a new drug or medical device, these AI tools can be deployed without clinical trials or safety checks. The call is growing for governments to treat medical AI like any other medical product and require proper vetting before it's used on patients.

sport.summary: Round 15 NRL is underway tonight with the Rabbitohs hosting the Broncos. The Origin selection debate is still raging, with Wayne Bennett giving a Latrell Mitchell update. In AFL, South Australia has locked in the Gather Round until 2029 and Gary Ablett Jr. is heading to the Hall of Fame. Nick Kyrgios had an emotional comeback win at a grass-court tournament.

stories.title: Wayne Bennett gives Latrell Mitchell update; Raiders struck by injury ahead of Round 15
stories.why_it_matters: Wayne Bennett has addressed the Latrell Mitchell Origin selection debate, giving an update on the South Sydney star's availability. The Raiders have also copped a painful injury setback heading into Round 15. No full article text available, but these are the two big team news stories shaping this weekend's games.

stories.title: The huge Origin call that divided the NRL world — what the numbers actually say
stories.why_it_matters: The controversial Origin selection call — likely around a key player being dropped or overlooked — has split the NRL world. Fox Sports digs into the actual stats to see if the numbers support the decision. Origin is the biggest stage in rugby league, so every selection call gets intense scrutiny. No full article text available for the specific player named, but this is the dominant NRL talking point this week.

stories.title: Casey McLean's Origin arrival is proof the next generation has arrived
stories.why_it_matters: The ABC has a feature piece on Casey McLean's State of Origin debut, framing it as a generational moment for Queensland rugby league. McLean's emergence signals a new wave of talent coming through, with the ABC arguing this is exactly what Origin needed for long-term excitement and relevance.

stories.title: SA locks in AFL Gather Round until 2029 — but venues still TBC
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia has officially committed to hosting the AFL Gather Round (the festival where all 18 clubs play in Adelaide over one weekend) through to 2029, making it a fixture on the AFL calendar. However, no final decision has been made on which venues will host the games — Adelaide Oval is the obvious choice but there's pressure to use multiple grounds. Good news for South Australian football fans and the local economy.

stories.title: Gary Ablett Jr. inducted into AFL Hall of Fame — teammates pay tribute
stories.why_it_matters: Gary Ablett Jr., widely regarded as one of the greatest AFL players ever, has been inducted into the AFL Hall of Fame. Teammates and former rivals have paid tribute, calling it long overdue. Ablett won two Brownlow Medals (the AFL's best-and-fairest award) and was a dominant force for Geelong and Gold Coast Suns across two decades.
